sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Nottingham Forest host Burnley at the City Ground with the model leaning home side (home 55%, draw 23%, away 22%; both teams to score 58%). Forest are 16th (33 points) and Burnley 19th (20). The stakes are high for both at the bottom end of the table.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Forest are unbeaten in 5 (3 wins, 2 draws), including a decisive away win at Tottenham and a controlled home win over FC Porto. Burnley are winless in 5 (1 draw, 4 losses), conceding 11 and scoring 4 in that run. Momentum favours the hosts.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: The last 2 meetings at Turf Moor finished 1-1 and 1-2 to Forest. Recent head-to-head trends show both teams often scoring, with matches generally tight on margins.

sections.subtitle: Season stats snapshot
sections.text: Forest have scored 32 and conceded 44, with 8 clean sheets and 5.4 corners per game. Burnley have scored 33 and conceded 63. It is a limited attack versus a defence that allow many goals.

sections.subtitle: Tactical notes
sections.text: Forest are effective in transitions and wide delivery, with Neco Williams adding consistent supply. Burnley rely on Jaidon Anthony’s direct threat and set-piece quality from James Ward-Prowse to create chances.

sections.subtitle: Key players
sections.text: Morgan Gibbs-White leads Forest’s end product (9 goals), while Matz Sels and Neco Williams are in form. For Burnley, Zian Flemming (8 goals) and Jaidon Anthony (strong recent output vs Forest) carry the main goal threat.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Thomas Kirk averages 4.5 yellow cards per game. Forest’s recent matches trend to fewer cards and under double-digit corners at home. Expect a moderate card count and corners around average.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Forest to edge a competitive match, with Burnley likely to create enough for a response. The hosts’ stronger form and home edge align with a narrow home win and both teams to score.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context and first-half summary
halftimeSections.text: Nottingham Forest trail 0-1 at the break at the City Ground after Zian Flemming finished late in the half. The home side controlled territory and entries but lacked precision in the box. Burnley were compact, took their one big chance, and protected the penalty area well.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key first-half numbers
halftimeSections.text: Possession: Forest 52% vs Burnley 48%. Expected goals: Forest 0.34 vs Burnley 0.04. Shots on target: Forest 1 vs Burnley 2. Final third entries: Forest 36 vs Burnley 19. Penalty area entries: Forest 12 vs Burnley 3. Corners: Forest 2 vs Burnley 1. Aerial duels won: Forest 36% vs Burnley 64%. Big chances created: Forest 0 vs Burnley 1.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical patterns
halftimeSections.text: Forest used width and early crosses, with Neco Williams the main supply line on the right. Chris Wood received service but Burnley’s centre-backs cleared effectively. Morgan Gibbs-White found space and produced Forest’s only effort on target. Murillo stepped in well from defence. Burnley sat in a mid-to-low block, broke through wide runners, and relied on quick transitions. Quilindschy Hartman created the decisive opening, while James Ward-Prowse screened the midfield and intercepted passing lanes. The away side’s aerial advantage helped them defend the box.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Forest started on the front foot. Burnley then enjoyed a clear spell around the middle of the half with several consecutive attacking waves. The final 15 minutes before the break were dominated by Forest pressure, but the goal arrived for Burnley just before half-time.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Cards and corners outlook
halftimeSections.text: First half produced no bookings and a 2-1 corner edge to Forest. Duels were even overall and there were no major flashpoints. Expect Forest pressure to lift corner volume after the restart, with Burnley’s aerial strength important when defending set pieces. Card count projects to stay low to moderate unless the game state becomes more stretched.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: Forest’s territorial control and penalty area presence suggest they are well placed to equalise. Key routes: quicker switches to Williams and Ola Aina for early deliveries, and more second-ball support around Wood to offset the away side’s aerial edge. Gibbs-White between the lines remains central. Burnley will look to compress the middle third, protect the half-spaces, and break through Flemming and Marcus Edwards. Set pieces for the away side remain a route to goal given their superiority in the air.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Next goal: Nottingham Forest. Most likely scorer: Chris Wood. Correct score prediction: 1-1. Forest have the stronger chance creation profile, but Burnley’s structure and set-piece threat should be enough to protect a point. Second half goal expectancy: moderate, with one goal more likely than two.
